players.product: AI colocation in retrofit data centers (NC-1 North Carolina 40 MW IT leased to Nscale; MTL-3 Montreal for Cerebras) plus GPU cloud services on NVIDIA B300 / Vera Rubin clusters

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K customer concentration: its Initial Customer (a cloud services customer, not named) accounted for approximately 70.7% of revenue in the 12 months ended December 31, 2025 and 96.6% of revenues through December 31, 2024; DNA Fund accounted for approximately 11.5% of 2025 revenue (no revenue in 2024). Services to the Initial Customer were paused and its GPUs redeployed to three other customers while the parties discussed a resolution of the service agreements. In data centers, MTL-1 and MTL-3 served fifteen customers and no one customer exceeded 50% of data center revenue; the Iceland HPC data center had contracts with twenty one customers in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: Initial Customer ~70.7% of revenue (2025), 96.6% (2024); DNA Fund ~11.5% (2025)

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's 10-K XBRL segment revenue for fiscal year 2025: cloud services $68.8M, +50.4% YoY vs $45.7M; colocation services $8.9M, +554.8% YoY vs $1.4M. Total revenue was $79,164,252 versus $47,639,237 in 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: cloud services $68.8M (+50.4% YoY); colocation services $8.9M (vs $1.4M); total revenue $79,164,252
